A1.justification: Despite retitling and substantial reorganization, both PDFs describe PBFM and the same physical benchmarks. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments on the unit-circle toy problem, Darcy flow, Kolmogorov flow and dynamic stall, including ablations and computational timings.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds baseline comparisons, sensitivity studies and method-variant results, including Appendix J.

M1.justification: The core ConFIG updates, unrolling, residual weighting, DiT architecture and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. V3 Appendix J introduces two tested variants: separating the physics residuals into distinct losses and backpropagating the residual loss only through the final unrolling step. These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Darcy, Reynolds-conditioned Kolmogorov, pitching-airfoil dynamic-stall and unit-circle tasks. Dataset populations, resolutions and conditioning ranges remain unchanged. The toy experiment moves from v2 Section 2.4 to v3 Appendix B; new sensitivity experiments use retained coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated DiffusionPDE and D-Flow comparisons across the PDE benchmarks, ECI on Darcy and PCFM on dynamic stall (Tables 2 and 4), including D-Flow's failed Kolmogorov evaluation. DM disappears from the Darcy comparison but remains in the toy experiment. FM-OT and the ConFIG-only variant match earlier FM and PBFM-1 terminology.

E3.justification: V3 adds Jensen-Shannon divergence, alternative Darcy normalization, sampler-threshold sweeps and dynamic-stall noise and gradient-flow protocols. New comparator settings include boundary-only ECI enforcement and D-Flow filtering at RE < 5, retaining 888 Darcy samples or 403 under alternative scaling. Original splits and training budgets remain unchanged. V3's conflicting Darcy MAE/MSE labels prevent an unqualified cross-version metric comparison.

E4.justification: V3 adds sampler-threshold, noise-level and normalization sensitivity studies, measured gradient conflicts/alignment, and separate-loss and final-step-backpropagation ablations (Tables 3, 5, 8 and 11–14; Appendices F and J). Earlier toy, architecture and loss-weighting analyses remain. V2's Darcy uniform-versus-logit sampling-time comparison in Figure 5 is removed, although corresponding toy variants remain.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 6 explicitly displays Kolmogorov residual variation across conditioning values using violin plots; v3 replaces this comparison with point metrics in Table 4. Sample/condition error bands remain elsewhere, including Figures 10 and 16. Neither version specifies independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive numerical baseline, sensitivity and variant results. For example, Table 4 reports dynamic-stall residual MSEs of 0.339e-6 for PBFM and 0.143e-6 for newly evaluated PCFM, with inference times of 60.47 and 3906 ms. Darcy and dynamic-stall training-time entries are exchanged between v2 Table 3 and v3 Table 6. These additions and revisions do not establish same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: Following the unchanged gradient-update equations, v3 replaces v2's assertion of equal positive gradient inner products with separate positivity conditions. It also adds approximate residual-MSE scaling with sigma_min squared and a dynamic-stall noise bound. The underlying flow-matching and PDE mathematics remains, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V2 foregrounds a novel physics-integrated flow-matching framework and up to eightfold residual improvement. V3 instead foregrounds first recognition of the physics–distribution trade-off and a Pareto-optimal balance, explicitly claiming that unrolling mitigates Jensen's gap. Presenting the approach as adapting established techniques also revises the headline novelty claim.

C2.justification: V3 explains unrolling through Jensen's gap, develops Pareto trade-off interpretations, and adds explanations involving deterministic-sampler bias, mode collapse and alignment between physics gradients. It adds memory-cost limitations and interpretations of normalization, noise and variant trade-offs. V2's explanation that numerical residual noise compensates for zero added Gaussian noise is omitted.

D1.justification: V3 adds Darcy normalization constants, comparator implementation disclosures, memory measurements and variant implementation details. Core optimizer, EMA, architecture and training hyperparameters remain unchanged, as does the code/data availability statement. V2's explicit pixel-independent 1D Wasserstein description and exact CPU model number are omitted, slightly reducing specificity.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around constrained generation, discussing FFM, ProbConserv, D-Flow, ECI, PCFM, PIDDM, PIRF and PCFT. New Table 1 contrasts constraint enforcement, inference gradients and loss balancing. Earlier topology-optimization discussions and citations are removed, while Jensen's-gap literature and the revised trade-off novelty claim become central.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanations and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before methodology, the toy ablation moves into Appendix B, and the conclusion becomes a discussion with explicit limitations. Terminology is revised throughout, including FM-OT and the renamed ConFIG-only variant.

P2.justification: V3 adds a gradient diagram, Pareto plot, method-comparison table and numerous quantitative, sensitivity and memory tables. Darcy plots are recombined, several histogram/violin displays disappear, and field comparisons lose some no-unrolling panels. The main dynamic-stall visualization is simplified, while many appendix plots are retained with relocation or relabeling.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens empirical support: conditional benchmarks previously compared mainly FM variants, whereas Table 4 adds external competitors and exposes accuracy–cost trade-offs. New sensitivity, gradient and variant analyses test important design choices, and memory reporting improves transparency. These gains outweigh remaining reporting weaknesses, including inconsistent Darcy MAE/MSE labels and prose reversing the Kolmogorov standard-deviation-error comparison in Table 4.
